Date: Wed, 15 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: DPA redline: retention / backups / erase window questions

Hannah,

Thanks for taking the DPA. We reviewed the redline from your legal team and have a couple of sticking points before we can move to counter-signing:

- Erase window: our security team is pushing for primary plus backups to be erased within 30 days after termination/contract expiration except for material legal hold. Your current language references a 90-day backup retention; we need tighter guarantees and evidence.
- Onshore backup carveouts: the redline allows for cross-region replicated snapshots for disaster recovery. We need clarity on whether onshore copies (for regulatory reasons) are considered 'backups' or a distinct class with a shorter retention.
- Proof of deletion: we require a certification of deletion (signed) and a manifest for affected tenant ids.

Attached is our annotated DPA (OptiHealth_DPA_redline_v3.docx). Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Laura

Laura — thanks for the clear note and the annotated doc. Looping in Marissa (AM) and Olga (legal) so we can align quickly. A couple of framing points from our side before we get into precise language: 

- Operational reality: we keep snapshots for disaster recovery and for rolling back in case of corruption. Those snapshots are typically immutable for short windows, and full deletion from cold backups can take longer than primary storage.
- What we can offer: we can separate 'Primary customer data' (user-facing and inference logs) and 'DR/backups' in the DPA. For primary data we can commit to 30 days post-termination to execute purge. For backups we typically operate on a 90-day schedule but are willing to negotiate a shorter exploitable compromise if we can define carveouts for: ongoing legal holds, active investigations, and disaster recovery windows.

Proposed next step: product + infra propose a middle-ground timeline, then legal redlines it. Are you available for a 30-minute call tomorrow? I'll circulate an initial compromise language after hearing from infra.

Thanks,
Hannah

Hannah — quick technical context from infra before the call: 

- Snapshot propagation: in our multi-region setup, snapshots are replicated asynchronously; depending on the datastore and the snapshot cadence, a tombstone/erase marker may take up to 14–28 days to fully propagate and be eligible for physical purge. That contributes to the longer backup retention timeline.
- Onshore copies: we can treat onshore replicas as a distinct retention class and enforce separate TTLs. However, the act of certifying physical purge for onshore copies requires a coordination window with the cloud provider and runbook ops (we have an internal playbook).

Suggested compromise language for redline (operational + legal friendly):
- Primary data: purge within 30 days of contractual termination (subject to legal hold).
- Onshore replicas: purge within 45 days of termination; Redwood will provide a deletion certificate and a manifest of affected tenant identifiers within 7 days of purge completion.
- Offsite DR/backups: longer-tail copies (archival/immutable snapshots) to be retained up to 90 days, except when specifically requested and paid-for expedited purge is agreed.

I'm attaching a short runbook excerpt that we can include as an exhibit if OptiHealth wants operational proof (erase-cert-playbook-draft.pdf).

Jonas/Hannah — appreciate the concrete framing and the runbook excerpt. A couple of follow-ups from our legal/security team: 

- 45 days for onshore replicas is acceptable if we get a signed deletion certificate and a tenant manifest within 7 days after purge completion (as proposed).
- For offsite DR/backups retained up to 90 days: can we get an option in the DPA to request an expedited purge for a fee (to be negotiated) and to receive a forensic snapshot prior to purge if needed for compliance?
- KMS: we require confirmation that customer-managed keys are supported for OptiHealth production tenants and that key revocation processes do not impede recording of a deletion certificate.

If you can confirm the above in redline language and share a counter-DPA, we can route to OptiHealth Legal and get back quickly. We are targeting signature before EoM November.

Laura / Marco — thanks, team. Per infra + legal alignment, attached is a concise counterproposal and a redline summary pulled into a single doc (redwood-dpa-counter-45day.docx). High-level summary below for your reviewers and OptiHealth Legal: 

- Primary data: 30 days purge window post-termination, subject to express legal hold carveout.
- Onshore replicas: 45 days purge window; Redwood will issue a signed deletion certificate and a tenant manifest within 7 business days of the recorded purge completion. Certificate will include keys of records deleted and the date/time stamp.
- Offsite DR/backups: default 90 days retention. DPA will include an 'expedited purge' clause: OptiHealth may request an expedited purge; Redwood will execute subject to a prescribed operational SLA (X business days) and an agreed fee schedule. Expedited purge will be accompanied by a pre-purge forensic snapshot, retained in a secure escrow for 30 days only if needed for compliance.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys in our Private and Dedicated deployments; for Hosted deployments we offer BYOK integrations with KMS providers and confirm that key revocation will not prevent generation of deletion certificates (we will record proofs and manifests under immediate retention). Specific KMS providers and key lifecycle steps will be enumerated in the exhibit.

Next steps: 1) Olga will push these redlines into the DPA and share a Google Doc for in-line comments (https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-redline-summary). 2) If OptiHealth accepts, we'll send a DocuSign packet (https://app.docusign.com/OPH-4521/redline). 3) Marissa will coordinate a short pilot for the purge flow with your infra team during the week of Nov 27 to validate the manifests and certificates.

Attaching: redwood-dpa-counter-45day.docx (counter redline), erase-cert-playbook-draft.pdf (ops exhibit).

Thanks — we aim to have the DPA signed quickly if this meets your legal/security bar.
